hello.note: The final は is read wa, not ha.

goodbye.note: Sounds final; day to day people say では、また (de wa, mata) or 失礼します (shitsurei shimasu).

please.note: For asking. When offering or inviting ("please, go ahead"): どうぞ (dōzo).

thank_you.text: ありがとうございます

youre_welcome.note: Often people just say いいえ (iie), "not at all".

yes.note: Also signals "I'm listening", not always agreement.

no.note: Can sound blunt; people soften it: いえ、大丈夫です (ie, daijōbu desu), "no, I'm fine".

sorry.note: Less formal than すみません (sumimasen), which is safer with strangers and at work. Among friends: ごめん (gomen).

excuse_me.note: Often preceded by あの (ano): あの、すみません. The same word also means "sorry".

good_morning.note: Among friends and family: おはよう (ohayō).

how_are_you.note: Asked after some time apart, not as an everyday greeting.

im_fine.text: 元気です、ありがとうございます
im_fine.note: A warmer, very Japanese reply: おかげさまで元気です (okagesama de genki desu).

whats_your_name.note: More polite: お名前を伺ってもいいですか (onamae o ukagatte mo ii desu ka).

my_name_is.note: Natives often drop 私は and just say …です. More formal: …と申します (… to mōshimasu).

nice_to_meet_you.note: Usually followed by よろしくお願いします (yoroshiku onegai shimasu).

where_from.text: どちらからいらっしゃいましたか？
where_from.note: Simpler: どこから来ましたか (doko kara kimashita ka).

im_from.note: Also common: …出身です (… shusshin desu).

speak_english.note: Softer: 英語は大丈夫ですか (eigo wa daijōbu desu ka).

speak_slowly.text: もう少しゆっくり話してください

where.note: On its own, どこ？ (doko?) is casual.

what.note: On its own, 何？ (nani?) is casual. 何 is read nan before です.

why.note: Also なぜ (naze), more formal, or なんで (nande), casual.

who.note: Politer: どなたですか (donata desu ka).

where_bathroom.note: Politer: お手洗いはどこですか (otearai wa doko desu ka).

can_you_help.text: 手伝っていただけますか？
can_you_help.note: For help with a task. If you are in trouble: 助けてもらえますか (tasukete moraemasu ka).

what_means.text: これはどういう意味ですか？
what_means.roman: Kore wa dō iu imi desu ka?

four.note: Also read shi, but yon is preferred: shi sounds like 死, "death".

seven.note: Also read shichi; nana is clearer and more common on its own.

nine.note: Also read ku, but kyū is more common on its own.

water.note: In restaurants people say お水 (omizu).

tea.note: Means green tea by default; black tea is 紅茶 (kōcha).

bread.note: Borrowed from Portuguese pão centuries ago.

menu_please.text: メニューをお願いします

bill_please.text: お会計をお願いします
bill_please.note: Also お勘定 (okanjō). In many places you pay at the register by the door.

delicious.note: Politer, e.g. to a host: おいしいです (oishii desu).

no_meat.note: Vegetarian: ベジタリアンです (bejitarian desu).

enjoy_meal.note: Said by those about to eat. A host inviting guests to eat says どうぞ召し上がってください (dōzo meshiagatte kudasai).

straight_ahead.note: Go straight on: まっすぐ行ってください (massugu itte kudasai).

stop_here.text: ここで止めてください
stop_here.note: Also very common: ここでお願いします (koko de onegai shimasu).

want_to_go.note: To a taxi driver: …までお願いします (… made onegai shimasu).

one_ticket.text: 切符を一枚お願いします
one_ticket.note: 一枚 (ichimai) is "one" for flat things such as tickets.

too_expensive.note: Haggling is unusual in most Japanese shops.

cheaper.text: もう少し安いのはありますか？
cheaper.roman: Mō sukoshi yasui no wa arimasu ka?

id_like_this.note: Also これにします (kore ni shimasu), "I'll take this one".

just_looking.note: In speech often shortened to 見てるだけです (miteru dake desu).

pay_card.note: Also common: カード使えますか (kādo tsukaemasu ka).

closed.note: Literally "preparing", the flip side of 営業中. Closed all day: 本日休業 (honjitsu kyūgyō).

tomorrow.note: Also read asu (a little formal) or myōnichi (very formal, e.g. business).

good_night.note: Before sleep; casual おやすみ (oyasumi). Leaving somewhere at night: 失礼します (shitsurei shimasu).

see_you_later.note: For the next day: また明日 (mata ashita).

wait_moment.text: ちょっと待ってください
wait_moment.note: Staff say the formal 少々お待ちください (shōshō omachi kudasai).

call_police.text: 警察を呼んでください！
call_police.note: The police number in Japan is 110, said hyakutōban.

need_doctor.text: 医者に診てもらいたいです
need_doctor.note: Literally "I'd like a doctor to see me". Urgent: 医者を呼んでください (isha o yonde kudasai).

dont_feel_well.note: Feeling sick or nauseous: 気分が悪いです (kibun ga warui desu).

pharmacy.note: Drugstores, ドラッグストア (doraggusutoa), also sell basic medicine.

hospital.note: Careful: 美容院 (biyōin) is a hair salon.

allergic.note: の is often dropped: 卵アレルギーがあります (tamago arerugī ga arimasu), egg allergy.

be_careful.note: As a sudden warning shout: 危ない！ (abunai!), "watch out!"

no_problem.note: More formal: 問題ありません (mondai arimasen).

maybe.note: Also かもしれません (kamo shiremasen) at the end of a sentence: "it might be".

dont_know.text: ちょっとわかりません
dont_know.note: ちょっと softens it. 知りません (shirimasen) also means "I don't know" but can sound curt.

i_like_it.note: About something just seen or received: 気に入りました (ki ni irimashita).

dont_like_it.text: あまり好きではありません
dont_like_it.note: あまり ("not very") softens it. Conversational: 好きじゃないです (suki ja nai desu).

im_tired.note: Past form, as in "I've got tired". Casual: 疲れた (tsukareta).

im_happy.note: Happy about something that just happened. Happy in life: 幸せです (shiawase desu).

welcome.note: Shops and restaurants greet customers with いらっしゃいませ (irasshaimase).

congratulations.text: おめでとうございます！

my_family.note: Natives usually say just 家族 (kazoku) or うちの家族 (uchi no kazoku).

mother.note: Your own mother, talking to others. Someone else's, or calling yours: お母さん (okāsan).

father.note: Your own father, talking to others. Someone else's, or calling yours: お父さん (otōsan).

brother.note: Your older brother. Younger: 弟 (otōto). Someone else's older brother: お兄さん (oniisan).

sister.note: Your older sister. Younger: 妹 (imōto). Someone else's older sister: お姉さん (onēsan).

child.note: Someone else's: お子さん (okosan). Son: 息子 (musuko); daughter: 娘 (musume).

friend.note: Same for men and women. More formal: 友人 (yūjin).

this_is_my_friend.text: こちらは私の友達です
this_is_my_friend.roman: Kochira wa watashi no tomodachi desu
this_is_my_friend.note: こちら (kochira) is the polite "this" for people. With a name: 友達の…です (tomodachi no … desu).

are_you_married.note: Politer: ご結婚されていますか (gokekkon sarete imasu ka). Quite personal with new acquaintances.

have_children.note: More respectful: お子さんはいらっしゃいますか (okosan wa irasshaimasu ka).

monday.note: Often shortened to 月曜 (getsuyō). 月 is the moon.

weekend.note: In speech also 土日 (donichi), "Saturday and Sunday".

what_day.note: Asking the date instead: 今日は何日ですか (kyō wa nannichi desu ka).

next_week.note: This week: 今週 (konshū); last week: 先週 (senshū).

eleven.note: Literally "ten one"; 12 to 19 work the same way.

hundred.note: Sound changes: 三百 (sanbyaku), 六百 (roppyaku), 八百 (happyaku).

thousand.note: Sound changes: 三千 (sanzen), 八千 (hassen). 10,000 has its own word: 一万 (ichiman).

how_old.note: Plainer: 何歳ですか (nansai desu ka), often used with children.

years_old.note: Sound changes: 一歳 (issai), 八歳 (hassai), 十歳 (jussai). Age 20 has its own word: 二十歳 (hatachi).

red.note: Before a noun: 赤い (akai), as in 赤い車 (akai kuruma), a red car.

blue.note: Before a noun: 青い (aoi). Also covers some greens: a green traffic light is 青信号 (aoshingō).

green.note: Takes の before a noun: 緑の車 (midori no kuruma). Also グリーン (gurīn).

what_colour.note: 何色 is read naniiro here; nanshoku would mean "how many colours".

this_one.note: Japanese has three: これ (near me), それ (sore, near you), あれ (are, far from both).

that_one.note: Far from both of you. If it is near the person you're talking to: それ (sore).

another_one.text: もう一つお願いします
another_one.note: For a drink: もう一杯お願いします (mō ippai onegai shimasu).

its_hot.note: ね (ne) invites agreement, like "isn't it". Hot to the touch is 熱い, also atsui.

its_cold.note: Cold to the touch, e.g. water or a drink: 冷たい (tsumetai).

its_raining.note: In speech often 降ってます (futtemasu).

its_sunny.note: Forecasts say 晴れ (hare); cloudy is 曇り (kumori).

its_windy.note: Literally "the wind is strong". Typhoon: 台風 (taifū).

weather_today.text: 今日の天気はどうですか？
weather_today.roman: Kyō no tenki wa dō desu ka?
weather_today.note: Weather forecast: 天気予報 (tenki yohō).

beautiful_day.note: A classic small-talk opener with neighbours and shopkeepers.

umbrella.note: Cheap clear ones from convenience stores: ビニール傘 (binīrugasa).

summer.note: Hot and muggy, as Japanese summers are: 蒸し暑い (mushiatsui).

winter.note: Spring is 春 (haru), autumn 秋 (aki).

have_reservation.note: With your name: 予約している…です (yoyaku shite iru … desu).

room.note: Staff say お部屋 (oheya). Room number: 部屋番号 (heya bangō).

luggage.note: Leaving bags at a hotel: 荷物を預かってもらえますか (nimotsu o azukatte moraemasu ka).

wifi_password.text: Wi-Fiのパスワードは何ですか？
wifi_password.roman: Waifai no pasuwādo wa nan desu ka?
wifi_password.note: Wi-Fi is written in Latin letters and read waifai.

check_out_time.text: チェックアウトは何時ですか？

map.note: Asking to be shown: 地図で教えてもらえますか (chizu de oshiete moraemasu ka).

next_train.text: 次の電車は何時ですか？
next_train.roman: Tsugi no densha wa nanji desu ka?
next_train.note: Bullet train: 新幹線 (shinkansen). Which platform?: 何番線ですか (nanbansen desu ka).

is_this_seat_free.text: この席は空いていますか？
is_this_seat_free.roman: Kono seki wa aite imasu ka?
is_this_seat_free.note: Simpler and very common: ここ、いいですか (koko, ii desu ka).

what_do_you_do.text: お仕事は何をされていますか？
what_do_you_do.roman: Oshigoto wa nani o sarete imasu ka?
what_do_you_do.note: Simpler: お仕事は何ですか (oshigoto wa nan desu ka).

i_work_in.note: For a place. For a field: …の仕事をしています (… no shigoto o shite imasu).

im_student.note: Same for men and women. University student: 大学生 (daigakusei).

office.note: Also 事務所 (jimusho). "At the office" is usually 会社で (kaisha de), "at the company".

meeting.note: Also ミーティング (mītingu), often for smaller, less formal meetings.

im_busy.note: Declining an invitation, softer: ちょっと用事があって (chotto yōji ga atte), "I have something on".

day_off.note: 明日は休みです (ashita wa yasumi desu): tomorrow is my day off. Paid leave: 有給 (yūkyū).

colleague.note: Same for men and women. In speech often 会社の人 (kaisha no hito), "someone from work".

lets_start.note: Casual: 始めよう (hajimeyō). Opening a meeting: それでは始めます (sore de wa hajimemasu).

good_job.note: Literally "just as expected of you". To a junior: よくやったね (yoku yatta ne).

table_for_two.note: Staff ask 何名様ですか (nanmeisama desu ka). 二人 (futari) is the special word for two people.

what_recommend.note: Menus often mark recommended dishes with おすすめ.

not_spicy.text: 辛くしないでください
not_spicy.note: Is it spicy?: 辛いですか (karai desu ka). No wasabi, at sushi places: さび抜きで (sabinuki de).

vegetarian_food.note: Many soups and sauces contain fish stock, だし (dashi), even without visible meat.

more_water.text: お水のおかわりをお願いします
more_water.roman: Omizu no okawari o onegai shimasu
more_water.note: おかわり (okawari) is a refill or second helping, also of rice or coffee. Water is free.

no_sugar.text: 砂糖なしでお願いします
no_sugar.note: No milk either: ブラックで (burakku de), "black". Unsweetened drinks are labelled 無糖 (mutō).

im_full.note: Turning down more food: もう結構です (mō kekkō desu). Casual: お腹いっぱい (onaka ippai).

takeaway.text: 持ち帰りでお願いします
takeaway.note: Also テイクアウトで (teikuauto de). Staff may ask お持ち帰りですか (omochikaeri desu ka).

it_was_delicious.note: When leaving, also ごちそうさまでした (gochisōsama deshita), "thank you for the meal".

keep_change.note: Tipping isn't customary in Japan, so this is rarely needed and may be politely refused.

stomach.note: The organ itself is 胃 (i), as in 胃が痛い (i ga itai).

head_hurts.note: Works for any body part: お腹が痛いです (onaka ga itai desu).

have_fever.note: Feeling a bit feverish: 熱っぽいです (netsuppoi desu).

medicine.note: Painkillers: 痛み止め (itamidome). Cold medicine: 風邪薬 (kazegusuri).

call_ambulance.text: 救急車を呼んでください！
call_ambulance.note: The ambulance and fire number in Japan is 119, said hyakujūkyūban.

dentist.note: Clinic signs usually say 歯科 (shika).

need_rest.note: Literally "I'd like to rest a little". Staying off work: 今日は休みます (kyō wa yasumimasu).

feel_better.note: Often with おかげさまで (okagesama de), "thanks to you", or だいぶ (daibu), "much".

get_well.note: Politer: お大事になさってください (odaiji ni nasatte kudasai).

lets_meet.note: 今度 (kondo) is "some time soon". Casual: また会おうね (mata aō ne).

are_you_free.text: 明日はお時間ありますか？
are_you_free.note: Also common: 明日は空いていますか (ashita wa aite imasu ka). Friends: 明日空いてる？ (ashita aiteru?)

call_me.note: More formal, e.g. at work: お電話ください (odenwa kudasai). Friends: 電話して (denwa shite).

your_number.text: 電話番号を教えていただけますか？
your_number.roman: Denwa bangō o oshiete itadakemasu ka?
your_number.note: Friends often swap contacts on LINE, Japan's main messaging app, instead.

have_nice_day.note: Less common than in English. Very common: よい週末を (yoi shūmatsu o), "have a nice weekend".

good_luck.note: Literally "do your best". Among friends: 頑張って (ganbatte).

happy_birthday.text: お誕生日おめでとうございます！
happy_birthday.note: Among friends: 誕生日おめでとう (tanjōbi omedetō).

thanks_a_lot.text: どうもありがとうございます
thanks_a_lot.note: For something already done, often ありがとうございました (arigatō gozaimashita).

miss_you.note: Literally "I want to see you". Also 寂しいよ (sabishii yo), "I feel lonely".
